claims.text: An ultrathin copper-philic layer can be deposited conformally on tungsten particles by atomic layer deposition.
Pre-depositing the ALD layer will enhance copper wetting on tungsten during sintering.
Pre-depositing the ALD layer will strengthen tungsten–copper interfacial bonding.
The ALD treatment will reduce void formation relative to vapor coating and mechanical alloying.
The ALD treatment will reduce W–Cu phase separation relative to vapor coating and mechanical alloying.
Conventionally powder-metallurgy-processed W–Cu materials, including vapor-coated W powders consolidated by SPS, typically exhibit interfacial voids and phase separation.
SPS and related powder-consolidation methods can operate below the melting points of the principal components.
The conformal ALD layer modifies tungsten surface energy and surface chemistry.
Modification of tungsten surface energy and chemistry promotes intimate W–Cu contact and diffusion bonding.
The ALD coating lowers the interfacial-energy barrier to copper wetting.
Improved wetting facilitates uniform copper diffusion into tungsten surfaces.
Better W–Cu interfacial contact minimizes voids and phase separation.
Reducing interfacial voids and phase separation preserves thermal conductivity under irradiation.
Reducing interfacial voids and phase separation preserves mechanical durability under irradiation.
Vapor-coated tungsten powders consolidated by SPS achieve near-perfect W–Cu interfacial contact.
Vapor-coated/SPS W–Cu baselines nevertheless exhibit microstructural heterogeneity and occasional void formation.
Relative to vapor coating or SPS, ALD-treated W–Cu will exhibit improved interfacial continuity, thermal transport, and mechanical integrity after irradiation.
The long-term effects of irradiation on the ALD-derived interfacial layer are not established.

contradictions.description: The material-initial-state field says vapor-coated W powders consolidated by SPS typically exhibit interfacial voids and phase separation, whereas the baseline describes the same general route as achieving near-perfect interfacial contact. Occasional voids can coexist with near-perfect contact, but the stronger 'typically' defective characterization is not reconciled.
